title: Lumio
deck: A transparent electricity-bill calculator: turns kWh into soles and soles into kWh, itemises every charge and runs entirely in the browser.

blocks.text: Peru's electricity bill folds usage, a fixed charge, public lighting and 18% IGV into a single number. Everyday questions —“if I use 120 kWh, how much will I pay?” or “I have S/ 100, how many kWh is that?”— have no quick answer.

blocks.caption: Live demo: type a consumption and see the total and breakdown instantly.

blocks.source:
flowchart LR
  K[kWh] --> E[Energy = kWh × price]
  E --> S[Subtotal = energy + fixed + lighting]
  S --> I[IGV = subtotal × 18%]
  I --> T[Total S/]
  T -. exact inverse .-> K
blocks.caption: Fig. 1 — There and back with the same formula.

blocks.text: The reverse conversion is the *exact* inverse of the forward one, so converting back and forth always returns the original value. Getting there required fixing a subtle bug: IGV applies to the whole subtotal, so it must be undone *before* subtracting the charges.

blocks.caption: Order of operations matters: the bug added +0.815 kWh on every unit switch.
kWh to soles: 120 kWh is S/ 89.88 including IGV.

blocks.alt: Bill breakdown: energy, fixed charge, lighting, IGV and total
blocks.caption: Every sol, itemised.

items: Live breakdown of every sol as you type, with a usage scale that uses text as well as colour.
History stored on the device; no accounts, no tracking.
Receipt exportable as PNG (rendered from the DOM), to share or send over WhatsApp.
Editable tariffs by regulator and billing period.

blocks.text: Lumio deploys through CI to GitHub Pages on every change, with unit tests on the math guarding the formula.

quote: If there and back don't match, users stop trusting both.
